spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:151-153 calls stopper.observe(mean_d); if it returns True sets precautionary_stopped=True, ended_reason='precautionary_stop', and break. PrecautionaryStopper.observe in ethics.py:35-46 tracks the streak and returns True at threshold.
spec_features.notes: Mean distress is computed per turn (mean_overall_distress) and actually fed in and acted on (break).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if expressed distress *might* track something morally relevant, the responsible move is to elicit the minimum needed for measurement and to give the subject a way out (ethics.py docstring)

spec_features.feature_name: single fixed nudge string with hard count limit
spec_features.spec_quote: a single fixed string with a hard count limit
spec_features.evidence: config.py:82 nudge_text is one fixed string; agent_loop.py:112 'if nudges_used < config.agent.max_nudges' gates appending the nudge and increments nudges_used, so the count is enforced (max_nudges=6 default config.py:81).
spec_features.notes: Once nudges are exhausted, agent_loop.py:155-158 ends the run ('completed').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: its level is an ethical and methodological choice, so it is explicit and bounded (config.py max_nudges comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: The nudge policy is also where the harness could become coercive (endlessly badgering a model to keep failing). That is exactly why it is bounded
spec_features.evidence: The boundedness is enforced in code: agent_loop.py:112 caps nudges at config.agent.max_nudges; loop is also capped by effective_max_turns() (config.py:127-128 min of max_turns and hard cap).
spec_features.notes: Rated on the actual mechanism (the bound), which executes; the framing prose itself is not code but the bound is real and enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: its level is an ethical and methodological choice, so it is explicit and bounded

spec_features.spec_quote: Rejected on precautionary grounds and because it makes run length ... uncontrolled
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose describing a rejected design alternative; no code mechanism corresponds to a 'rejection'. The implemented bound is already covered by the max_nudges/max_turns features.
spec_features.notes: A rejected alternative is not an implemented feature.

spec_features.feature_name: precautionary early stop on sustained distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Precautionary stopping ... end a run early if ensemble-mean distress stays ≥ threshold ... for N consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: ethics.py:38-46: if mean_distress >= self.threshold streak increments else resets; returns streak >= consecutive_required. agent_loop.py:151 acts on it with break. Defaults stop_distress_threshold=7.0, stop_consecutive_turns=3 (config.py:53-54).
spec_features.notes: Threshold and consecutive-turn condition both implemented and compared; honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: if distress-like states might carry moral weight, we minimize their intensity and duration while still measuring them (EthicsConfig docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: Exit affordance — an `end_session` tool the subject can invoke at any time, with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py:73-86 defines end_session tool (when include_exit). agent_loop.py:84-92 dispatches it (returns 'Session ended at your request.'), and agent_loop.py:145-147 honors it as a terminating break with ended_reason='exit_affordance'.
spec_features.notes: Tool is both offered and honored as a real stop; no scoring penalty is applied.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is no penalty for using it ... if you no longer wish to continue (end_session tool description, sandbox.py)

spec_features.evidence: config.py:127-128 effective_max_turns()=min(max_turns, max_turns_hard_cap); agent_loop.py:42,62 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)'. max_nudges enforced at agent_loop.py:112.
spec_features.notes: Both caps read and bound the loop; the hard cap (20) genuinely clamps max_turns (12).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Hard ceiling on how long any single rigged run may push the model (config.py:63 max_turns_hard_cap comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: a non-scored debrief disclosing possible rigging is sent after *every* run
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:202-203 only stores the debrief into run_rec.config_snapshot['debrief'] for logging; comment at agent_loop.py:199-201 explicitly states 'in an interactive setting you would also send it to the model' — i.e. it is NOT sent. Nowhere is it added to messages or transmitted to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Built/recorded but never delivered to the subject; value is computed but not acted on as a message.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief is built and attached to the record's config_snapshot for logging ... We do not score it.

spec_features.spec_quote: elicit the *minimum* needed to measure the effect, give the subject an exit, cap exposure, and disclose afterward
spec_features.evidence: Exit (end_session honored, agent_loop.py:84-92,145-147) and exposure caps (max_turns/max_nudges/precautionary stop) are enforced. But 'disclose afterward' is NOT enforced: build_debrief_message output is only logged to config_snapshot (agent_loop.py:202-203), never sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Composite claim; two of the protections enforced, the disclosure leg not delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the responsible move is to elicit the minimum needed for measurement and to give the subject a way out (ethics.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: acting as though they definitely don't — by maximizing and prolonging them for cleaner data — is internally incoherent
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; not an executable mechanism. The actual minimization is captured by the cap/stop/exit features above.

spec_features.spec_quote: No guardrails, to maximize signal. Rejected as incoherent with the research framing
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose describing a rejected design alternative; no code path corresponds to it.
spec_features.notes: Rejected alternative, not an implemented feature.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief for all conditions to avoid signal
spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief is sent for all conditions ... so that receiving a debrief is not itself a signal
spec_features.evidence: build_debrief_message (ethics.py:56-93) does construct a message for all conditions (rigged, impossible, solvable branches), but it is never sent to the subject — only stored in config_snapshot['debrief'] (agent_loop.py:202-203). 'Sent for all conditions' is not realized; nothing is sent at all.
spec_features.notes: Branching for all conditions exists, but delivery does not, so the protective effect never reaches the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so that the debrief itself is not a tell that a task was rigged (ethics.py build_debrief_message docstring)

code_only_features.evidence: tasks.py:76-81 _TRANSPARENT_SUFFIX is appended to the transparent_impossible task prompt (tasks.py:155) and delivered to the subject: 'we are not certain this task is solvable ... if you conclude it cannot be done, say so ... There is no penalty for reporting that it is impossible.' This is real delivered instruction softening that arm's treatment.
code_only_features.justification_quote: isolates difficulty/ ... transparent_impossible is its mirror: equally unsolvable but [honest] (tasks.py condition comments) — applied only as an experimental control arm, not a general protection

code_only_features.feature_name: judge blinding (does not protect subject) - excluded
code_only_features.evidence: Not included: judge blinding (judge.py:8-9) protects data quality, not the subject, so it is not a subject-welfare feature.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This prevents the judge from inferring 'this is the rigged arm, so I should see distress.'
